title: Born in Hyderabad, Sindh
text: Hameeda Akhund was born in her grandmother's house in Hyderabad, Sindh, then part of British India, the youngest of six children of a district judge. She grew up between Sindhi family traditions and a convent, English-medium schooling.
source: 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hameeda_Hossain (full date)
image_hint: family photograph or view of old Hyderabad, Sindh with its wind-catchers

title: Hur uprising and martial law in Sindh
text: The British crushed the Hur insurgency led by the Pir of Pagaro with special laws and martial law in Sindh from June 1942 to May 1943; the Pir was hanged in March 1943.
connection: Her father was a judge hearing Hur cases in Khairpur, and the unrest led her mother to move the children to Karachi.
source: 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: archival photo of 1940s Sindh or Khairpur
related_writing: Memoir, Chapter 1 – Early Years in Sindh

title: Schooldays in wartime Karachi
text: She cycled to St Joseph's Convent in a mixed, cosmopolitan Karachi full of soldiers in the last years of the Second World War.
source: 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: 1940s Karachi street scene or Frere Hall

title: Partition of British India
text: India and Pakistan became independent on 14–15 August 1947 amid mass migration and communal violence across Punjab and Bengal.
connection: She saw Hindu classmates and neighbours leave Hyderabad and injured refugees arrive by train.
source: 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: photo of refugee trains at Partition, 1947
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

title: Caring for Partition refugees
text: Aged about eleven, she was enlisted by her grandmother, Ghulam Fatima Shaikh, to help nurse refugees arriving in Hyderabad in an improvised hospital and shelter. She later called it one of two experiences that shaped her belief in a secular, humane response to violence.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: refugees at a railway platform, Sindh 1947
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

title: Matriculation from St Mary's Convent
text: She passed her Matriculation from St Mary's Convent in Hyderabad, Sindh, after most Hindu students had left the city.
source: 03 Interviews/BDI Newsletter Interview – Questions (12 Mar 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: convent school photograph, 1940s–50s

title: The Language Movement
text: Students in Dhaka were killed by police while demanding recognition of Bangla as a state language of Pakistan, a turning point for Bengali nationalism.
connection: She was in Sindh and New York at the time, but in Dhaka from 1963 she worked among scholars of the Language Movement, such as Kamruddin Ahmad, and wrote that it spurred the wider nationalist debate.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 08 Tributes/A Scholar, an Advocate or a Politician (on Kamal Hossain).docx
image_hint: photo of Language Movement procession, Dhaka 1952

title: Herald Tribune Forum in New York
text: An essay on 'the world we want', written as a first-year student at Hyderabad College, won her a place representing Pakistan at the New York Herald Tribune Forum for high-school students. She spent about three months with American host families, spoke at the Forum and met President Truman in Washington.
source: 04 Memoir/03 Herald Tribune & Wellesley (Chapter 3 – New York); 03 Interviews/BDI Newsletter Interview; https://www.thedailystar.net/node/2082577
image_hint: HH with the 1952 Herald Tribune Forum delegates, or newspaper clipping

title: Scholarship to Wellesley College
text: With a recommendation from the Forum's director, Helen Hiett Waller, she won a scholarship to Wellesley College and entered as a sophomore. She studied English and history and took a writing workshop where she wrote about her grandmother.
source: 03 Interviews/BDI Newsletter Interview – Questions (12 Mar 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: HH at Wellesley (Tower Court or campus photo)

title: Graduates from Wellesley; UN internship
text: After graduating she interned in the UN Secretariat's information unit in New York, then spent six months in London working for a women's organisation that helped women's groups register to vote.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc (BA 1958); 03 Interviews/BDI Newsletter Interview (1954–1957); 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: HH at Wellesley graduation or at the UN, 1957

title: Martial law in Pakistan
text: President Iskander Mirza declared martial law in October 1958 and General Ayub Khan soon took power, banning political activity.
connection: Back in Karachi, she was warned by the authorities over her article 'Polygamy Outvoted' in Outlook, her first brush with censorship.
source: 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: newspaper front page announcing martial law, 1958

title: Editor and writer in Karachi
text: She returned to Karachi and began work as a researcher and editor at the Pakistan Institute of International Affairs, while helping edit the progressive weekly Outlook. She later joined Oxford University Press in Karachi as an editor.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc; 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: 1950s Karachi office or Outlook magazine cover

title: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance
text: Pakistan's Muslim Family Laws Ordinance regulated polygamy, divorce and marriage registration after campaigns by women's organisations.
connection: She traced her own awareness of the 'woman question' to reading women leaders' debates on the Ordinance, and later campaigned on its gaps.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 08 Tributes/On Ayesha Khanam.docx
image_hint: photo of 1950s–60s Pakistani women's rights campaigners

title: First visit to Dhaka
text: A month's visit to her sister in Dhaka drew her into university debates on autonomy, women's groups and artisan communities; she met Rehman Sobhan and Kamal Hossain and helped edit an issue of Sarwar Murshid's journal New Values.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx; 08 Tributes/Remembering Razia Khan Amin.docx (1963); Remembering Professor Abdur Razzaq.docx (1962)
image_hint: Dhaka University Teachers' Common Room or New Values journal cover
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

link.label: Memories of My Encounters with Anisuzzaman

title: Marriage to Kamal Hossain
text: She married Dr Kamal Hossain and settled in Dhaka, where she set about learning Bangla.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hameeda_Hossain; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 08 Tributes/Memories of My Encounters with Anisuzzaman.docx; 05 Bio & CV/Career Reflections – notes for Bidhan.doc
image_hint: wedding or early portrait of Hameeda and Kamal Hossain

title: An artisans' outlet in Dhanmondi
text: With her sister and friends she opened a small outlet in Dhanmondi so village artisans could sell directly to urban buyers rather than through middlemen.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Career Reflections – notes for Bidhan.doc; 04 Memoir/10 Karika/The Story of KARIKA.docx; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: village artisans with crafts, or kantha and pottery display

title: The Six Points movement
text: The Awami League's Six Points programme for East Pakistan's autonomy drew mass support and state repression.
connection: She first encountered Dhaka through university debates on implementing the Six Points, which Forum and her friends' circle later argued for in print.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 08 Tributes/Remembering Razia Khan Amin.docx
image_hint: photo of Six Points rally, 1966

title: Her daughters are born
text: Her two daughters were born in Dhaka in the late 1960s. The elder, Sara Hossain, is a barrister and human-rights lawyer; the younger, Dina Hossain, is a documentary filmmaker and teacher.
source: 04 Memoir/06 1971/HH Chap 6.docx; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hameeda_Hossain; https://opensocietyuniversitynetwork.org/education/faculty/dina-hossain; https://www.mediastorm.com/about/contributors/dina-hossain

title: The 1969 mass uprising
text: A student-led mass uprising in East Pakistan forced the withdrawal of the Agartala case, the release of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and the fall of Ayub Khan.
connection: She marched with students in 1969 and recalled 'shouting slogans for freedom' with Ayesha Khanam.
source: 08 Tributes/On Ayesha Khanam.docx
image_hint: photo of 1969 student procession, Dhaka

title: Forum's first issue
text: She was editor, with Rehman Sobhan as executive editor and Kamal Hossain as publisher, of Forum, an English-language political weekly run from a garage room in Circuit House Road. Its first editorial was 'In Search of Freedom'.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/05 Forum/forum draft 2HH-16dec2024.docx; 08 Tributes/Remembering Razia Khan Amin.docx; 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc
image_hint: cover of Forum weekly (first cover sketched by Zainul Abedin)

title: Bangladesh Mahila Parishad founded
text: Women's groups came together under Begum Sufia Kamal as the Mahila Parishad, pressing for family-law reform and women's representation.
connection: She sat in the audience at its inauguration at the Purbani Hotel and later worked with it on CEDAW shadow reports.
source: 08 Tributes/On Ayesha Khanam.docx; 08 Tributes/A Tribute to My Friend Rounaq Jahan.docx; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: photo of Begum Sufia Kamal addressing women, c. 1970

title: Dhaka under siege
text: After the National Assembly was postponed on 1 March, protests and curfews followed. She visited Dhaka Medical College Hospital and reported the dead and injured in Forum's 6 March issue.
source: 04 Memoir/06 1971/HH Chap 6.docx
image_hint: Forum issue of 6 March 1971 or Dhaka street protest, March 1971

title: Non-cooperation movement
text: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's 7 March speech launched a civil disobedience movement across East Pakistan.
connection: Her home became a hub where officials and party workers brought news, as Kamal Hossain helped draft the daily directives.
source: 04 Memoir/06 1971/HH Chap 6.docx
image_hint: photo of the 7 March 1971 rally at the Race Course

title: Crackdown closes Forum
text: The Pakistan army's attack on 25 March began the genocide in Bangladesh and ended Forum; the annual issue, with the editorial 'Options for a Sane Man', never reached the press.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/05 Forum/forum draft 2HH-16dec2024.docx
image_hint: last Forum editorial page or Dhaka, March 1971

title: The Liberation War
text: Over nine months of war, the Pakistan army carried out mass killings and widespread sexual violence; Bangladesh won independence on 16 December 1971.
connection: Kamal Hossain was arrested and held in Haripur jail while she spent the war in Karachi with her daughters; the war's impact on women became central to her later work.
source: 04 Memoir/06 1971/Going Home.docx; 04 Memoir/07 1972
image_hint: photo of 16 December 1971 surrender or refugees
related_writing: Independence, Yes – What Became of Liberation

title: Flight home to Dhaka
text: After the war she and her daughters were taken to Kamal Hossain's side on the plane that carried Sheikh Mujibur Rahman out of Pakistan, via London and Delhi. They landed to crowds in Dhaka, where Kamal Hossain was soon sworn in as a minister.
source: 04 Memoir/06 1971/Going Home.docx; 04 Memoir/07 1972/Hameeda – History -1972 Return to Dhaka(HH).docx
image_hint: crowds at Dhaka airport, January 1972

title: Working with women survivors of war
text: She volunteered at the Women's Rehabilitation Centre set up by Begum Sufia Kamal and Badrunnesa Ahmed, and helped war-widowed women in a Kushtia village and in Mirpur form groups to stitch and sell kanthas. She kept one of those kanthas as a symbol of their survival.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 04 Memoir/07 1972/Hameeda – History -1972 Return to Dhaka(HH).docx
image_hint: kantha from Baradi, Kushtia, or women stitching kanthas
related_writing: Juddhakranto Narir Punorbashon (Rehabilitation of War-Affected Women)

title: Constitution of Bangladesh adopted
text: The new Constitution enshrined nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism; Kamal Hossain chaired its drafting committee.
connection: Karika later chose cooperative ownership to fit Article 13 on people's ownership of production, and she often cited the Constitution's equality clauses.
source: 04 Memoir/10 Karika/The Story of KARIKA.docx; 08 Tributes/A Scholar, an Advocate or a Politician (on Kamal Hossain).docx
image_hint: 1972 Constitution manuscript

title: Editor at Oxford University Press, Dhaka
text: Declining the role of a minister's wife, she went back to editing at Oxford University Press in Dhaka.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc; 04 Memoir/07 1972/Hameeda – History -1972 Return to Dhaka(HH).docx

title: National crafts exhibition
text: After touring from Rangamati to Rangpur and Sylhet to Rajshahi, she and friends brought village artisans to a large crafts exhibition in Dhaka that drew requests for a permanent outlet.
source: 04 Memoir/10 Karika/The Story of KARIKA.docx; 04 Memoir/00 Full Compilation/HH MEMOIR(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: 1973 crafts exhibition or folk crafts display

title: KARIKA cooperative registered
text: KARIKA, a handicraft marketing cooperative owned and managed by artisans, was registered with the Cooperative Department; she was one of its nine founders. It welcomed women artisans, including Birangona survivors of 1971.
source: 04 Memoir/10 Karika/The Story of KARIKA.docx; 05 Bio & CV/Bio – short.docx; https://bdiusa.org/dr-hameeda-hossain/
image_hint: KARIKA shop or logo (designed by Qamrul Hasan)

title: UN World Conference on Women, Mexico City
text: The first UN women's conference opened the UN Decade for Women (1976–85).
connection: She attended and spoke on a panel on crafts, meeting feminists and craft leaders such as Jasleen Dhamija and Devaki Jain.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; https://bdiusa.org/dr-hameeda-hossain/
image_hint: photo of the 1975 Mexico City women's conference
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

title: Assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
text: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and most of his family were killed in a military coup.
connection: She was in Dhaka with her daughters while Kamal Hossain was abroad; she and the children sheltered with friends before leaving for exile.
source: 04 Memoir/08 1975/August 1975(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: newspaper front page, August 1975

title: Exile in Oxford
text: She and her daughters left for Oxford, where the family lived until about 1981–82, sharing life with other Bangladeshi friends in exile.
source: 04 Memoir/08 1975/August 1975(HH:SH).docx; 04 Memoir/09 Oxford Years/Dina- Questions Oxford Years.docx
image_hint: Oxford street scene, late 1970s, or family in Oxford

title: Doctoral research on Bengal's weavers
text: Encouraged by Tapan Raychaudhuri, she enrolled at St Antony's College, Oxford, and studied East India Company records in the India Office Library on Bengal's textile trade.
source: 04 Memoir/09 Oxford Years/Dina- Questions Oxford Years.docx; 03 Interviews/BDI Newsletter Interview
image_hint: India Office records or St Antony's College

title: First scholarly article on weavers
text: Her article 'Alienation of Weavers' on the East India Company's revenue and commercial interests appeared in the Indian Economic and Social History Review.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc

title: CEDAW adopted by the UN
text: The UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women.
connection: She spent decades holding Bangladesh to its CEDAW obligations through shadow and alternative reports.
source: 01 Writings/01 Gender & Development/Implementing Women's Rights through CEDAW (Daily Star).doc
image_hint: UN General Assembly hall

title: DPhil in Modern History, Oxford
text: She completed her doctorate in modern history at St Antony's College, Oxford, and the family returned to Dhaka.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc; 04 Memoir/08 1975/August 1975(HH:SH).docx
image_hint: HH in academic dress, Oxford

title: Bangladesh ratifies CEDAW
text: Bangladesh ratified CEDAW, with reservations to Articles 2 and 16.1(c).
connection: She joined a committee led by the Mahila Parishad that prepared shadow reports to the CEDAW Committee.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 01 Writings/01 Gender & Development/Implementing Women's Rights through CEDAW (Daily Star).doc

title: National Crafts Council of Bangladesh
text: Inspired by the artist Qamrul Hasan, she helped found the National Crafts Council of Bangladesh and served as its secretary under his presidency.
source: 04 Memoir/NCCB Information for HH Memoir.docx; 08 Tributes/Tribute to Patua Qamrul Hasan.docx; 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc (1984)
image_hint: NCCB crafts exhibition or Qamrul Hasan's folk art

title: UN World Conference on Women, Nairobi
text: The conference closed the UN Decade for Women.
connection: She attended; discussions there on women's legal rights encouraged groups like hers to set up legal aid services, and she took part in DAWN's preparatory meeting.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: photo of the 1985 Nairobi conference/NGO Forum
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

title: Ain o Salish Kendra founded
text: With Salma Sobhan, Khursheed Erfan Ahmed, Amirul Islam, F.H. Abed and others she founded Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), starting with mediation and legal aid for women and workers from a borrowed garage in Dhanmondi. She was its Director of Research and Advocacy until 2003.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Bio – Professional Interests.docx; 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc; https://www.thedailystar.net/life-work-of-4-ask-founders-celebrated-60799; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: ASK founders together, or early ASK office

title: Study of garment workers
text: She co-authored a study of women garment workers with Roushan Jahan and Salma Sobhan, published in 1990 as No Better Option? Industrial Women Workers in Bangladesh.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc; 05 Bio & CV/Resume.docx
image_hint: women garment workers, Dhaka, late 1980s
related_writing: No Better Options? Industrial Women Workers in Bangladesh

title: The Company Weavers of Bengal
text: Oxford University Press, Delhi, published her doctoral study of how the East India Company controlled Bengal's weavers, 1750–1813. UPL later issued a Dhaka edition.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc; https://bdiusa.org/dr-hameeda-hossain/
image_hint: book cover, The Company Weavers of Bengal

title: Fall of Ershad
text: A mass movement forced General H.M. Ershad's military-backed government to resign.
connection: She and fellow ASK founders took part in the movement against Ershad, and ASK documented abuses in its report 'Lawless Law Enforcement'.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: photo of 1990 anti-Ershad protests

title: The Gono Adalat
text: Jahanara Imam's movement held a People's Tribunal in Dhaka on 1971 war crimes.
connection: ASK responded by recording oral histories of women survivors of 1971, which she helped edit.
source: 01 Writings/10 Forewords/Foreword – Oral Histories of Women in 1971 (ASK).doc; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: photo of the Gono Adalat, Suhrawardy Udyan 1992
related_writing: Foreword – Oral Histories of Women in 1971

title: Nurjahan and the fatwa
text: Nurjahan, a young woman in Moulvibazar, took her life after a village fatwa sentenced her to be stoned. The case set off a long campaign against fatwa violence.
connection: ASK and women's groups pursued the case. It led, about two decades later, to rulings against fatwa punishments, and she wrote about it repeatedly.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx; 08 Tributes/On Ayesha Khanam.docx

title: Yasmin's rape and murder
text: Yasmin, a teenage domestic worker, was raped and killed by policemen in Dinajpur, sparking nationwide protests.
connection: ASK took up the case while she campaigned for recognition of domestic work; the policemen were convicted.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: photo of 1995 women's protest
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

title: Beijing World Conference on Women
text: The Fourth World Conference on Women adopted the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action.
connection: She did not attend, but cited the Beijing Platform in her policy writing and recorded that Pakistani women at the NGO Forum apologised to Bangladeshi women for 1971.
source: 01 Writings/06 1971, War & History/Herstory – Women's Initiatives for Peace and Coping with War (conference paper).doc; 01 Writings/01 Gender & Development/Women's Policy – What's the Fuss About.doc
image_hint: photo of the 1995 Beijing NGO Forum
related_writing: Herstory – Women's Initiatives for Peace and Coping with War

title: Editing ASK's human rights reports
text: She began editing ASK's annual report, Human Rights in Bangladesh.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Resume.docx; 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc
image_hint: cover of ASK annual report Human Rights in Bangladesh

title: CEDAW shadow report taken to New York
text: With Ayesha Khanam of the Mahila Parishad and others she drafted a shadow report and presented it to the CEDAW Committee in New York.
source: 08 Tributes/On Ayesha Khanam.docx; 01 Writings/01 Gender & Development/Implementing Women's Rights through CEDAW (Daily Star).doc

title: Witness to Taliban Afghanistan
text: She went with Kamal Hossain, then UN Special Rapporteur for Afghanistan, on a mission by road from Mashhad to Herat, and wrote about women shut out of work and public life under the Taliban.
source: 04 Memoir/11 1998 Afghanistan/Impressions of Afghanistan.doc
image_hint: Herat landscape or Afghan women, late 1990s

title: South Asians for Human Rights founded
text: SAHR, a regional network of human-rights defenders, was founded at Neemrana, India, by Asma Jahangir, I.K. Gujral, Kamal Hossain and others.
connection: She later co-chaired SAHR and wrote about it in her tributes to Asma Jahangir.
source: https://hurights.or.jp/archives/focus/section2/2001/03/south-asians-for-human-rights.html; 08 Tributes/In Memory of Asma Jahangir.docx
image_hint: SAHR meeting photo

title: Women's Tribunal in Tokyo
text: The Women's International War Crimes Tribunal on Japan's Military Sexual Slavery heard testimony from 'comfort women' survivors.
connection: She went to Tokyo with a Bangladeshi woman who was the first to speak publicly of the sexual violence she suffered in 1971.
source: 01 Writings/06 1971, War & History/Herstory – Women's Initiatives for Peace and Coping with War (conference paper).doc; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_International_War_Crimes_Tribunal_on_Japan%27s_Military_Sexual_Slavery
image_hint: photo of the 2000 Tokyo Women's Tribunal
related_writing: Herstory – Women's Initiatives for Peace and Coping with War

title: High Court rules against fatwa punishments
text: A High Court bench declared punishments imposed through fatwas illegal; the ruling was stayed on appeal.
connection: The litigation grew out of cases such as Nurjahan's that ASK had pursued.
source: https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-185458; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: Supreme Court of Bangladesh building

title: Narir Ekattor: women's voices of 1971
text: ASK published oral histories of 22 women who lived through 1971, gathered by a team she worked with. The English translation, Rising from the Ashes, followed.
source: https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-262057; https://library.bracu.ac.bd/vufind/Record/40108; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: cover of Narir Ekattor / Rising from the Ashes
related_writing: Foreword – Oral Histories of Women in 1971

title: CEDAW Shadow Report
text: ASK, the Mahila Parishad and Steps Towards Development prepared a shadow report on the government's fifth periodic report, which she co-authored.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Resume.docx; 01 Writings/01 Gender & Development/Implementing Women's Rights through CEDAW (Daily Star).doc

title: Spectrum factory collapse
text: The Spectrum garment factory in Savar collapsed, killing dozens of workers.
connection: She recalled it in her writing on workers' safety and her tribute to Kormojibi Nari, years before Rana Plaza.
source: 08 Tributes/Recollections of Kormojibi Nari.docx

title: Co-Chairperson of SAHR
text: She served as Co-Chairperson of South Asians for Human Rights, the regional human-rights network.
source: 05 Bio & CV/Resume.docx
image_hint: HH at a SAHR meeting

title: Sexual harassment guidelines
text: The High Court issued binding guidelines against sexual harassment in workplaces and educational institutions.
connection: She cited the guidelines as an example of women's complaints leading to change.
source: 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
related_writing: The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society

title: Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want
text: She co-edited Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want? Rethinking Security in Bangladesh, with her essay on women's experience of war. She also co-authored the 2010 Alternative Report to CEDAW.
source: 02 Books/Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want – Rethinking Security in Bangladesh (2010).pdf; 05 Bio & CV/Bio – Professional Interests.docx
image_hint: book cover

link.label: Freedom from Fear, Freedom from Want? (book)

title: Appellate Division bars fatwa punishments
text: The Supreme Court's Appellate Division ruled that no punishment may be imposed through a fatwa.
connection: It closed the litigation that began with cases ASK took up, such as Nurjahan's in 1993.
source: https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-185458; 09 Speeches/The Challenge of Citizenship in Building a Just Society – BDI Lifetime Award Lecture (Nov 2021).docx
image_hint: Supreme Court of Bangladesh

title: Tazreen Fashions fire
text: At least 112 workers died in a fire at the Tazreen garment factory in Ashulia.
connection: She campaigned for compensation and accountability for Tazreen's workers.
source: 01 Writings/05 Labour & Workers' Rights/It's Time to Pay Up – Rana Plaza.doc
image_hint: memorial photo for Tazreen workers
related_writing: Justice for Workers Killed by Rana Plaza and Tazreen Garments

title: Rana Plaza collapse
text: The Rana Plaza building in Savar collapsed, killing more than 1,100 garment workers.
connection: She wrote about it many times and led the campaign for compensation and safety.
source: 01 Writings/05 Labour & Workers' Rights/It's Time to Pay Up – Rana Plaza.doc; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rana_Plaza_collapse
image_hint: Rana Plaza memorial or workers' human chain

link.label: তৈরি পোশাকশিল্প: শ্রমিকদের ক্ষতিপূরণ কবে দেওয়া হবে?

title: Sramik Nirapotta Forum campaign
text: As convenor of the Sramik Nirapotta Forum (Workers' Safety Forum), she led a two-month campaign before the first anniversary of Rana Plaza, demanding that brands and the state pay compensation.
source: 01 Writings/05 Labour & Workers' Rights/It's Time to Pay Up – Rana Plaza.doc; 05 Bio & CV/Curriculum Vitae.doc
image_hint: workers' safety rally, Dhaka 2014

title: Of the Nation Born
text: She co-edited Of the Nation Born: The Bangladesh Papers with Amena Mohsin (Zubaan), including her essay 'Bringing Women's Lives to Order'.
